spec.slice: WS03 S8 v2: parking (park write at a round boundary, park-aware recovery worker, park resume through the one /continue route). Design only, against the committed tree on branch model-plane (HEAD ad322122, working tree clean apart from the untracked .plan-work/). Function names are cited, not line numbers. All Model Plane paths are under "apps/Model Plane"; the BFF and the SPA are under "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3".
spec.summary:
S8 turns a small set of typed, content-free, recoverable stops of a root Do loop into a durable park. A park is an encrypted kind "park" fold written at a round boundary, and RunAgentResponse.status is "parked" with park_reason. A parked run is resumed through the existing POST /continue route by a body with a claim_token and no approval. Parking is an upgrade of a failure and never a new way to fail: if the park cannot be written for any reason, the run gets exactly the committed outcome (same reply, same typed failure_code, same terminal receipt).

Decision table (pinned runs only in the first merge, per P5):
- These stops park:
  - loop-top DeadlineCause::Credential -> credential_window, park_until now.
  - latched or round refusal subscription_usage_limit -> provider_exhausted. park_until is resets_at, else now + retry_after_ms, else now + 300 s.
  - rate_limited with retry_after_ms -> provider_exhausted, park_until now + retry_after_ms.
  - subscription_upstream_unavailable -> upstream_unavailable, park_until now + retry_after_ms, else now + 60 s.
  - subscription_reauth_required -> reauth_required, park_until now.
- These stay failures: WallClock, rate_limited without timing, subscription_bad_request, prompt_too_long, subscription_route_unavailable (typed or the generic fallback), RouteUnavailable, Exhausted, every unpinned untyped failure, and the post-loop latched refusal (no budget left).
- crash_interrupted is written only by the session-core worker.

Executor side:
- A new pure module runtime_loop/park.rs.
- A FoldWriter::save_park that is a fenced save: exactly one RPC at the writer's expected seq, no probe, no tombstone.
- RoundsOutcome::Parked, returned by run_agent_with_route before finalize and before the sandbox lease release.
- A third continuation stage "park", in addition to segment and loop. It pre-claims the parked fold with an EMPTY pause_ref inside run_agent_with_tools. It then:
  - rebuilds the route from the fold extensions route_model and route_connection_id;
  - re-derives the deadline from the new request's bearers;
  - checks the offered tools and the prompt digest against the fold;
  - seeds run_rounds with RoundSeed::Parked through the one FoldWriter::seeded call site;
  - saves the fence (save_fence at the claimed seq) BEFORE the first inference.

Session-core side:
- save validates a park: it must sit at a round boundary, name its own park, have parks in 1..=5, have park_until <= now + SESSION_CORE_PARK_TTL_SECONDS, and SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED must be on.
- claim gains an empty-ref branch for kind = 'park' rows (parked, or resuming with a lapsed lease). It never matches a pause fold. It does not touch updated_at, which stays the TTL anchor, and it renews the obligation deadline in the same transaction.
- The recovery worker gets decide_hold, recovery_hold and park_crashed, dormant unless both SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED are on.
  - Spare: a parked fold within the TTL, or any fold with a live claim.
  - CrashPark: only an active fold of kind 'round', with no open round, no pending approval row of any expiry, no ledger row reserved at or after its updated_at and no open reservation, under the cap, restorable, and carrying route identifiers when pinned. It is re-sealed under seq+1, so a zombie writer gets loop_checkpoint_stale.
  - Terminalize: everything else, through the unchanged apply_managed_terminal_outcome (outcome_unknown, reconciliation_required, fold purged in the same transaction).
- S8-0 lands first as a separate commit: the has_pending_approval expires_at fix, in both copies (the claim_due_recovery candidate query and has_pending_approval).

Wire:
- RunAgentResponse.park_reason = 11. Verified free: the message ends at resets_at = 8, plan 4.3 reserves 9 and 10, and nobody has 11.
- OrchestrationEvent RunParked = 24 and RunResumed = 25. Verified free: the highest tag is 23, and 4.3 reserves 24/25 for WS03 S8.
- RunDetail.resumable/park_reason 17/18 are committed and reused unchanged.
- Raw SSE frame run_parked with exactly {run_id, reason, retry_after_ms?, resets_at?}.
- Two new closed executor and frame tokens: park_not_restorable and park_route_unavailable.

The BFF and the SPA get display-only handling and the park-aware Continue contract. The contract (action-registry chat.run.continue plus chat-run-continue-contract.ts) lands before the gateway accepts the shape. No UI button is wired.

Every switch is default-off. With all switches off the runtime behaviour is that of the committed code, with two recorded exceptions: the BFF accepts an absent approval_id key (a 422 today), and park saves by a non-S8 caller are refused while park recovery is off.
spec.approach:
VERIFIED STATE THAT S8 BUILDS ON (read from the committed source)

execution-core runtime_loop:
- fold.rs
  - WriterGate{switch, ledger, zdr, waived, space, depth, resumed} and WriterGate::decide.
  - FoldWriter::new / seeded. seeded forces resumed=false and seeds SeqTracker::seeded(expected_seq) and segment_no.
  - save_round, save_pre_effect, save_fence and fence_with: one RPC at tracker.expected(), no probe, ContentRefused is an error.
  - pause_fold and PauseFold::save.
  - Snapshot and build_fold. build_fold writes extensions only {effect_ledger: true}.
  - fit: scrub_fold plus to_bytes, one clear_stale_tool_results retry.
  - save_rpc: hard-codes park_reason "" and park_until None.
  - classify_status.
  - SaveKind{Round, PreEffect, Pause}: there is no Park.
  - close_rpc, GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT, prompt_digest_of.
- resume.rs
  - select_stage(mode, ...): only "loop" can be InPlace.
  - classify_claim, fence_refusal, in_place_writer_off.
  - check_fold: refuses kind != "pause" as FoldKindMismatch, "park is a later slice".
  - reconcile and restore_in_place_with: the claim pause_ref is format!("{run_id}:{step_id}").
  - Refusal: 10 closed tokens.
  - effective_authority: refuses req.provider_hint != paused.provider_hint as authority_route_mismatch.
  - apply_authority, offered_authority, ClaimedFold, Restored.
- agent.rs
  - run_agent: merged_tool_defs(req.tools ...).
  - run_agent_with_tools: ModelRoute::resolve(req, Switches::from_env(), EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL, caller), then RunDeadline::for_run(.., route.is_pinned(), bearers ..).
  - run_agent_with_route: begin_continuation, then apply_authority, then heartbeat_managed_agent_run, then LoopContext, then run_rounds, then the outcome match. Paused returns early; otherwise finalize, then release_sandbox_lease_if_any.
  - Continuation{release: ApprovedRelease (not Option), step_prefix, goal, seed, tools, mode, effective}.
  - RoundSeed{Segment, InPlace}.
  - writer_gate(req, route, ledger, depth, holds_release, in_place).
  - run_rounds:
    - The loop top checks ctx.route.is_stopped(), then ctx.refusal.latched() (outcome InferFailed(Some)), then ctx.deadline.expired() (any cause gives OutOfTime), then heartbeat, then rounds_executed += 1.
    - The inference Err arm uses refusal_for_failed_round for pinned runs only, latches when refusal.latches(), and returns InferFailed.
  - The subagent outcome match is exhaustive over RoundsOutcome.
- grpc.rs enforce_resume accepts mode "segment"|"loop" with a non-empty approval_id and claim_token; anything else gets invalid_argument "resume_incomplete".
- RunAgentResponse literals: 22 across agent.rs, model-gateway sse.rs, model-gateway tests/continue_preconsume_test.rs and e2e_invoke_chain_test.rs, and mp-contracts tests/proto_wire_parity_execution.rs. None uses ..Default.

session-core:
- loop_checkpoint.rs
  - save: kind park already requires pause_ref, park_reason and park_until, and ParkReason::parse (S4).
  - claim: UPDATE .. WHERE pause_ref = $4 AND (state IN ('paused','parked') OR (state='resuming' AND claim_expires_at < now())) .. updated_at = now(). The held check uses pause_ref = $3.
  - close, purge_run, check_fold, run_owner_tx (runs FOR UPDATE).
  - record_event payload is {seq, kind}.
  - scope_aad(run, org, user, seq) is private.
- terminalization.rs
  - claim_due_recovery: NOT EXISTS approvals requested/granted with consumed_at NULL, ignoring expires_at.
  - has_pending_approval: the same.
  - recover_claimed_terminalization: lock_run_status, lock_managed_obligation, has_pending_approval (spare via release_recovery_for_activity, ACTIVITY_RETRY_SECS 60), then apply_managed_terminal_outcome(Failed("outcome_unknown"), true).
  - transition_managed_run_terminal purges the fold.
  - supersede_terminalized_obligations runs at the start of every pass.
- orchestration_store.rs: CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL and DECIDE_APPROVAL_SQL honour expires_at, so an expired approval can never be consumed or granted. RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL and renew_recovery_deadline are private.
- run_service_grpc.rs
  - RUN_SELECT, fold_is_claimable, may_read_park_reason, row_to_detail. Already done: resumable and park_reason for kind park, reason only for the owner or a service.
  - cancel_run: UPDATE runs to cancelled, purge_run, a RUN_CANCELLED event, one transaction. It does NOT touch the obligation; supersede_terminalized_obligations ends it on the next worker pass, and so does a later heartbeat.
- tool_ledger: request_id is always the run id (effect::reserve), so a ledger row has NO per-attempt owner. A worker can only tell from reserved_at and status whether the ledger holds actions a fold does not account for.

model-gateway sse.rs:
- continue_run: continuation_gate, continue_persistent_gate, a blank approval_id or claim_token gives 400 continue_incomplete, then bearers, owner, GetRun, GetApproval, continue_preflight, resume_mode_for, run_agent_request_is_buildable, continue_resume (the ONE AgentResume literal), then the launch with AgentRoute::default() and spawn_consume_then_launch.
- CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS (10), CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS (17), CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS (22).
- AgenticRunOutcome{Completed, Failed, AwaitingApproval, Unknown}.
- orchestration_event_to_sse, orchestration_event_to_step_update and event_payload_value are exhaustive over the oneof.
- http_routes run_detail_value is an allowlist that deliberately never carries resumable or park_reason (test run_detail_value_never_carries_resumable_or_park_reason). S8 keeps it so.

BFF and SPA:
- BFF ContinueRunBody{approval_id, claim_token} with deny_unknown_fields; continue_upstream_body; CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS (8).
- ag_ui.rs: a CUSTOM list.
- SPA chatRunContinueInput{runId, approvalId min(1), claimToken}; continueRun sends {approval_id, claim_token}.

(1) PARK WRITE (execution-core)

park.rs, new and pure except try_park and the publishers:
- parking_active(): mp_contracts::loop_fold::loop_parking_enabled() && loop_resume_enabled(). Parking is pointless where nothing can resume. A ParkSwitch thread-local test override copies fold::CheckpointSwitch.
- park_reason_for(stop: &ParkStop) -> Option<ParkReason>, where ParkStop = {CredentialDeadline, WallClock, Refusal(&Refusal)}. The mapping is the table in the summary.
- park_until_for(reason, retry_after_ms, resets_at, now). Defaults: DEFAULT_PARK_SECS = 300 and SHORT_THROTTLE_PARK_SECS = 60 (P4).
- parkable(ctx facts) is true only when all of these hold:
  - depth == 0;
  - !req.zdr and !route.is_waived();
  - req.space_id is empty;
  - route.is_pinned() (P5: the first merge parks pinned runs only);
  - the writer is active (FoldWriter::is_active);
  - no seeded round is pending (a continuation's seeded first round has not run; parking there would drop the consumed release from the fold);
  - rounds used < max_rounds;
  - parks_so_far < MAX_PARKS_PER_RUN.
- park_ref = mp_contracts::loop_fold::park_ref(run_id, parks+1) = "park:{run_id}:{n}".

try_park(ctx, &mut folds, snapshot, stop) -> Option<ParkedRun>:
- Returns None at its first line unless parking_active() and parkable().
- Builds the fold:
  - build_fold(snapshot, None, Some(PendingPause{kind: Park, pause_ref: park_ref, step_id: "", call: "", action_fingerprint: ""}));
  - extensions parks = n+1;
  - route_model and route_connection_id, which snapshot.route already carries under parking.
- Calls folds.save_park(fold, reason, park_until).
- On Ok(seq) it publishes RunParked best-effort and returns Some(ParkedRun{reason, park_ref, seq, retry_after_ms, resets_at}).
- On any Err it returns None, and the caller falls through to its committed return.

The three decision sites in run_rounds, root only:
- A. In the ctx.refusal.latched() branch, before the committed return: try_park with the latched refusal and rounds_executed unchanged.
- B. In the ctx.deadline.expired() branch: try_park only for DeadlineCause::Credential, after the committed warn line.
- C. In the inference Err arm, after the latch: try_park with the round's refusal (pinned only) and a snapshot rounds_executed of rounds_executed - 1 (the failed round never produced a response), messages unchanged.

Outcome:
- Some(p) returns RoundsResult{outcome: RoundsOutcome::Parked(p), ..}.
- run_agent_with_route returns Ok(park::parked_response(..)) in the arm beside Paused. That is before finalize and before release_sandbox_lease_if_any; the lease follows its own TTL, as for Paused. The StateStore is untouched.
- The subagent match gets a Parked(_) arm that is unreachable (depth 0 only) and is handled like InferFailed(None).
- parked_response: status "parked", final_output "", rounds_executed = total, grounded, compaction_triggered, failure_code "", retry_after_ms, resets_at (label), park_reason = reason.as_str().

fold.rs additions:
- SaveKind::Park ("park", GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT).
- save_rpc gains park: Option<(&str, prost_types::Timestamp)>; every committed caller passes None, so the request is unchanged.
- FoldWriter::save_park(&mut self, fold, reason: ParkReason, park_until) -> Result<u64, SaveError>, built like fence_with:
  - an inactive writer gets Err(Unavailable{ambiguous: false}) and no RPC;
  - fit errors are returned (no tombstone);
  - exactly one RPC at tracker.expected(), kind park, pause_ref = fold.pending.pause_ref, park fields set;
  - no probe; on_saved or on_failed plus apply.
- Snapshot gains parks: u32 (restored from the seed's fold, 0 for a fresh run) and route: Option<RouteIds{model, connection_id}>. route is Some only when parking_active(), from ctx.route.model() and subscription_connection_id().
- build_fold inserts EXT_PARKS only when parks > 0, and the route extensions only when route is Some. With parking off every fold is byte-identical to the committed one; the golden fixtures loop-fold-v1-writer-*.json are unchanged.
- Every fold of a run under parking carries the route identifiers (identifiers, never credentials), so a crash-park of a pinned run can be resumed (P2).

(2) SESSION-CORE

S8-0 (separate first commit, terminalization.rs plus compose, P8):
- New fn park_recovery_enabled(): SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED, strict "true", plus a thread-local test override like loop_checkpoint::test_switch.
- Both the claim_due_recovery candidate NOT EXISTS and has_pending_approval gain: AND (NOT $honour_expiry OR a.expires_at IS NULL OR a.expires_at > now() OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM approval_delivery_outbox d WHERE d.approval_id = a.id AND d.state = 'processing' AND d.lease_expires_at > now())).
- $honour_expiry = park_recovery_enabled(). With it false the SQL selects the same rows as committed. The delivery clause keeps a cold delivery that leased the approval before its expiry from being terminalized mid-delivery.
- It is gated (P11) because it is a recovery-worker behaviour change, and park recovery depends on it: an expired approval must not shield a park forever. Whether to ship it ungated is listed as open.

loop_checkpoint.rs (store):
- park_ttl_seconds(): SESSION_CORE_PARK_TTL_SECONDS, default 86400, clamped to [60, 2_592_000], invalid falls back to the default.
- save for kind park adds, after the committed checks:
  - !park_recovery_enabled() gives failed_precondition "park_recovery_disabled". A park nothing will spare would only turn a typed failure into a later outcome_unknown, so the executor falls back.
  - fold.round_in_flight is Some, or fold.pending is not Park with pause_ref == input.pause_ref, gives invalid_argument "park fold must be at a round boundary and name its park".
  - parks_in(fold) not in 1..=MAX_PARKS_PER_RUN gives failed_precondition "park_limit_reached".
  - park_until > now + ttl gives failed_precondition "park_until_beyond_ttl".
- record_event payload gains park_reason for kind park only.
- claim: when pause_ref is "", a separate CLAIM_PARK_SQL. Every non-empty ref keeps the committed statement text.
  - Lock order: run_owner_tx (runs FOR UPDATE), then SELECT .. FROM managed_run_terminalization_outbox WHERE run_id = $1 FOR UPDATE, then the fold CAS. This is the worker's own order: runs -> outbox -> fold.
  - The CAS: UPDATE .. SET state = 'resuming', claim_token_hash, claim_expires_at WHERE run_id = $1 AND kind = 'park' AND (state = 'parked' OR (state = 'resuming' AND claim_expires_at < now())). It never matches a paused or pause-kind row, and it does NOT touch updated_at, which stays the TTL anchor.
  - On a win, RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL (made pub(crate) in orchestration_store) in the same transaction, so the gap until the executor's first heartbeat is covered whatever the recovery switch says.
  - The held check for an empty ref: kind = 'park' AND state = 'resuming' AND token match AND a live lease.
  - On a park claim, Claimed gains pause_ref (from RETURNING) for the log and RunResumed.
- park_crashed(tx, cipher, row) lives here because it needs scope_aad:
  - opens with AAD seq N and runs check_fold;
  - sets pending Park park_ref(run, parks+1) and extensions parks+1;
  - to_bytes (credential gate);
  - seals under seq N+1;
  - UPDATE .. SET seq = N+1, kind = 'park', state = 'parked', pause_ref, park_reason = 'crash_interrupted', park_until = now(), ciphertext, fold_digest, claim fields NULL, updated_at = now() WHERE run_id AND seq = N;
  - record_event CHECKPOINT_SAVED {seq N+1, kind park, park_reason};
  - any error returns Ok(false), and the caller terminalizes.

park_recovery.rs (new, worker policy):
- enum RecoveryHold{Terminalize, Spare, CrashPark}.
- Pure decide_hold(row: Option<&HoldRow>, facts: &CrashFacts, now, ttl, active: bool):
  - !active, or no row, or closed: Terminalize.
  - resuming with a live claim: Spare.
  - kind park and (parked, or resuming with an expired claim):
    - updated_at + ttl > now: Spare;
    - otherwise Terminalize.
  - paused, or resuming pause-kind with an expired claim: Terminalize. A paused fold holds the run only through its approval, which has_pending_approval already checked; one whose approval is consumed, denied or expired can never resume.
  - active and kind = 'round' and every crash fact clean: CrashPark. The crash facts:
    - no approval of the run in requested/granted with consumed_at NULL, of ANY expiry;
    - no session_tool_audit_intents row with reserved_at >= fold.updated_at;
    - no row with status 'reserved';
    - the fold opened and passed check_fold;
    - fold.is_resumable(), effect_ledger extension true, round_in_flight None, pending None;
    - messages[0] is system;
    - parks_in < MAX;
    - authority.provider_hint empty, or the route_connection_id extension present.
  - every other active fold, including pre_effect folds, every fence fold and every open round: Terminalize.
- recovery_hold(tx, run_id, ttl): SELECT state, kind, seq, pause_ref, updated_at, claim_expires_at FROM run_loop_checkpoints WHERE run_id = $1 FOR UPDATE, plus the two fact queries.

terminalization.rs recover_claimed_terminalization:
- After the pending-approval spare: if loop_checkpoint::enabled() && park_recovery_enabled(), call recovery_hold.
  - Spare: release_recovery_for_activity, commit, Ok(false).
  - CrashPark: DescriptorCipher::from_env() (a missing key is Terminalize), then park_crashed. On true: release_recovery_for_activity, commit, metric mp_session_loop_crash_parks_total, Ok(false). On false: Terminalize.
  - Terminalize: the unchanged apply_managed_terminal_outcome, plus mp_session_loop_park_ttl_terminalized_total when the row was kind park.
- With either switch off no fold query runs: the committed path, byte-identical.
- apply_managed_terminal_outcome, transition_managed_run_terminal and insert_managed_run_terminal_event are not modified.

(3) PARK RESUME

grpc.rs enforce_resume:
- if resume.mode == "park" && loop_parking_enabled():
  - require approval_id, step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint and brief empty, and claim_token non-empty;
  - otherwise invalid_argument "resume_incomplete".
- else: the committed check. With parking off, "park" is resume_incomplete exactly as today.

run_agent_with_tools, park path only (resume.mode == "park"), before the route is used:
- a. The request names no route: provider_hint and subscription_connection_id empty, else authority_route_mismatch. req.space_id empty, else authority_space_mismatch. caller.zdr_waiver is None, else durable_mutation_forbidden. A widened request is refused, not narrowed.
- b. The switches: parking_active() && fold::checkpoint_enabled() && effect::ledger_enabled(), else continue_disabled. And in_place_writer_off(writer_gate(req, &route0, ledger, 0, false, true), session_bearer.is_some()) must be None, else not_resumable. All of this is decided before any claim.
- c. park::claim_parked(session_channel, bearer, run_id, claim_token): ClaimLoopCheckpoint{pause_ref: "", claim_token}. Its status is classified by park::classify_park_claim:
  - claim_held -> continue_in_progress.
  - run_ended or not_claimable -> not_resumable.
  - PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated -> resume_forbidden.
  - The ZDR trailer -> durable_mutation_forbidden.
  - disabled -> continue_disabled.
  - "did not authenticate" or InvalidArgument -> park_not_restorable.
  - Anything else, including a timeout that may have committed -> resume_checkpoint_unavailable. A same-token retry gets continue_in_progress for the 120 s lease and then re-claims the lapsed park.
- d. Pure park::check_park_fold(claimed, run_id) runs, in order:
  - kind park, the fold's run, segment == fold.segment_no;
  - is_resumable;
  - the effect_ledger extension;
  - system first;
  - claimed.authority_digest == fold.authority.digest();
  - pending is Park with a pause_ref;
  - round_in_flight None;
  - rounds_executed + delegated < resolved max_rounds;
  - authority.space_id empty.
  A failure is a STRUCTURAL failure: best-effort close_rpc(seq, "park_not_restorable") so the worker terminalizes it honestly at the next due pass, then refuse park_not_restorable.
- e. park::route_request(req, fold): req.model = the route_model extension; if authority.provider_hint is non-empty, provider_hint = PROVIDER_ID and subscription_connection_id = the route_connection_id extension (missing gives park_route_unavailable); plan_mode = fold.authority.plan_mode. Then ModelRoute::resolve(&route_req, Switches::from_env(), EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL, caller). Err, a provider_hint different from fold.authority.provider_hint, or is_waived() gives park_route_unavailable. There is NO close (the cause can be transient, such as the kill switch): the lease lapses and the park can be resumed again. It never falls back to a default route (P2).
- f. The names of the offered tools (run_agent's merged_tool_defs over the request's empty client tools) must equal fold.authority.tool_names, and prompt_digest_of(compose_system_prompt(names), tools) == fold.prompt_digest. A failure is park_not_restorable WITHOUT close (deploy or policy skew can be transient).
- g. effective = effective_authority(&fold.authority, &route_req) and apply_authority. mode = resolve_mode(fold.authority.mode).
- h. deadline = RunDeadline::for_run(now, wall clock, route.is_pinned(), the NEW request's bearers ..), so a credential_window park resumes under fresh credentials.
- i. run_agent_with_route(.., route, deadline, Some(ParkClaim{..})). The new trailing parameter is None at every committed call site.

begin_continuation:
- The ParkClaim short-circuit: no consume, no select_stage.
- It returns Continuation{release: None (the field becomes Option<ApprovedRelease>), step_prefix: format!("s{segment}."), with segment = fold.segment_no + 1, goal: req.goal (not read), seed: RoundSeed::Parked(Box<ParkSeed>), tools, mode, effective}.
- It logs loop_resume_stage{resume_stage: "park"}.

run_rounds:
- in_place = matches!(seed, InPlace(_) | Parked(_)).
- Messages, counters, attempted_retrievals (the final set: a round boundary), children_started, grounded, compaction_triggered and parks come from ParkSeed. There is no seeded round and no slots; the system prompt and skills are not fetched again.
- The ONE FoldWriter::seeded call takes (claimed_seq, segment) from either seed.
- Immediately after the writer is built and before the while loop, for a Parked seed only: folds.save_fence(build_fold(snapshot, None, None)).
  - Err gives Err(fence_refusal(error).status()), with nothing inferred or dispatched.
  - Ok publishes RunResumed{run_id, segment_no, park_reason} best-effort.
- The fence moves the row to active at seq+1, fences a second claimant of a lapsed lease (it gets Stale and resume_checkpoint_unavailable), and closes the zombie window. The rest of the loop is the committed loop. The ordinary pre_effect save fences each later effectful round, and the loop may park again (parks carried forward and capped).

Gateway continue_run:
- After continue_persistent_gate: if req.approval_id.trim().is_empty() && loop_parking_enabled() && !claim_token blank, take the park branch. Otherwise the committed flow (continue_incomplete unchanged).
- The park branch, in order:
  - bearers (missing_bearer);
  - require_durable_run_owner_with_token;
  - GetRun;
  - continue_turn_gate(continue_after_approval_enabled(), persistent);
  - loop_resume_enabled(), else continue_disabled;
  - not ended, else not_resumable;
  - detail.resumable && ParkReason::parse(detail.park_reason).is_some(), else not_resumable;
  - run_agent_request_is_buildable;
  - continue_resume("", claim_token, PARK_RESUME_MODE), still the one AgentResume literal, segment_no 0;
  - launch with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent, without spawn_consume_then_launch and with no consume.
- No new HTTP code.

(4) WIRE

risks: The UI cannot see parks. run_detail_value deliberately excludes resumable and park_reason, crash parks emit no live event (P5), and no button is wired (P10). So a crash-parked run is visible to no user and lives up to the TTL (24 h) before ending outcome_unknown, where the committed code ends it about 15 minutes after the last heartbeat. Mitigation: SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED stays off until a UI path exists; the TTL can be shortened.

A loop that is alive but silent for more than 15 minutes can be crash-parked under itself. Today it is terminalized under itself. The seq+1 re-seal fails its next save (round saves are skipped, pre_effect saves are held, the writer fails), so it dispatches no further effect. Its read tools and inference can continue, and it can still finalize the run, which purges the park. A resume racing that zombie is fenced by its own fence save.

The ledger has no per-attempt owner (request_id is always the run id), so P6's 'release row owner' check is implemented conservatively as no ledger row reserved at or after the fold's updated_at, no open reservation, and never a pre_effect or fence fold. This refuses some crash-parks that would have been safe.
Tool-definition or prompt drift (a deploy, a policy view, the WIDE_RESEARCH switch) makes a parked run unrestorable: park_not_restorable, without a close, until the TTL.

An ambiguous park save (timeout) can commit while the executor falls back and finalizes. The terminal transition purges the fold in the same transaction, so the end state is the committed failure, but a CHECKPOINT_SAVED park event remains in the audit trail.

Lock order. A park claim takes runs, then outbox, then fold (the worker's order); the save path takes runs then fold; cancel takes runs then fold. claim_due_recovery locks outbox rows without the runs row, but only for one autocommit statement, so no cycle is formed. This is verified by reading, not by a stress test.
A usage limit that resets after the TTL (a weekly limit, for example) is refused at save and fails as today: parking helps short windows only.

The BFF has no switch, so an absent approval_id key changes from 422 to a forwarded park body. With the gateway's parking off that ends as a 400 model_error. This is accepted like S7c-A5, because no UI calls the route.

Gateway/executor skew: an executor that parks behind a gateway that does not know 'parked' reaches the Unknown arm (RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED) while the run is in fact parked. The deploy order puts the gateway first.

The recovery worker is safety-critical. All new logic sits in one pre-terminalize branch behind two switches, and the receipt functions are unchanged. The added queries run only for due runs, under locks the worker already holds.
Sandbox leases are not released on a park (as for Paused). A long park may meet WorkspaceStateLost, which the S7 closers already handle.
invariants: A park is an upgrade of a failure. If the park fold is not durably written for any reason, the run's outcome is exactly the committed outcome: same reply, failure_code, timing, one finalize and one receipt.

Only typed, content-free evidence parks: DeadlineCause::Credential, a closed trailer code, or the worker's own row state. No status message is ever parsed; rate_limited parks only with retry_after_ms; WallClock never parks.

Zero-retention, waived, Space, delegated and stage-1-segment runs never park, never keep a fold, and are never claimed or resumed. execution-core refuses before any RPC, and session-core refuses again (run_owner_tx retention, refuse_zdr_continuation).
A park sits at a round boundary: round_in_flight None, and no effect in flight. session-core refuses a park fold with an open round.
A park returns before finalize: no terminal receipt, no assistant message, no ledger finalization, no lease release.
An empty pause_ref claims only a kind = 'park' row (parked, or resuming with a lapsed lease), never a pause fold. One parked fold per run (primary key run_id).
A park resume saves its fence at the claimed seq before the first inference and before dispatching any call. A lost fence infers and dispatches nothing.
A park resume never runs on a default route. The route is rebuilt from the fold's identifiers through ModelRoute::resolve, or the resume is refused park_route_unavailable.
A widened /continue is refused, never narrowed: a park request that names a route, a Space or an approval is refused.
There is exactly one AgentResume literal in the gateway, and segment_no 0 is sent and ignored. The stage is chosen only by AgentResume.mode.

Crash-park covers only an active round-kind fold with no open round, no approval row (of any expiry) pending, and no ledger row the fold does not account for. A fold whose approval is consumed is never crash-parked or restored by a park resume.

Immutable receipts: TTL expiry and every non-spared case go through the unmodified apply_managed_terminal_outcome (one RUN_TERMINAL; the purge in the same transaction). Spare and CrashPark never write terminal state.
The lock order is runs -> outbox -> fold for the worker and for the park claim. The save, claim and cancel paths all take the runs row first.

With every S8 switch off, behaviour is the committed behaviour: no park RPC, no fold extension added, the committed claim SQL for every non-empty ref, no worker fold query, no new frame. The two recorded exceptions are the BFF absent-key form and park saves while park recovery is off.

Park, event, frame and log fields are ids, counts, closed tokens and timestamps only. Folds stay ciphertext under AAD (run, org, user, seq), are scrubbed and credential-gated, and the route identifiers are not credentials.
The Model proposes and Quarry executes: parking never touches browser_agent or Quarry state.

amendments_to_prior_specs: The resume path is now designed, which lifts the s8-parking.json NO-GO. P1: an empty-ref claim for kind = 'park' rows, plus the park-aware /continue with mode park and no approval, plus the contract first. P2: route re-pinning from fold extensions. Open questions 1, 2 and 8 of v1 are closed.

P1 is refined. The empty-ref claim also re-claims a park whose claim lease lapsed (resuming with kind still park). Without that, a resume that died between claim and fence would strand a run that RunDetail reports as resumable. It still never matches a pause fold.

The empty-ref claim does not refresh updated_at (TTL anchor) and renews the obligation deadline in its own transaction (RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL made pub(crate)), with the lock order runs -> outbox -> fold.

The original's LoopSnapshot is replaced by the committed fold::Snapshot plus build_fold (reconcile), extended with parks and route, which are written only under parking. FoldWriter::save_park is a fenced one-RPC save, not a save_bytes call with a probe.

parking_active requires EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED as well as the new EXECUTION_LOOP_PARKING_ENABLED: a park nothing can resume is not an upgrade of a failure. session-core also refuses a park save while SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED is off.
A new parkable guard: no park while a continuation's seeded first round is pending, because the loop top runs before the seeded round and a park there would drop the consumed release.
Unpinned parking and the guard_credentials widening are removed (P5). The inference-core provider_chain_exhausted trailer and its execution-core reader are removed from the first merge.
The RunDetail projection and the park_reason token validation are removed (already committed in S4). run_service_grpc.rs gets tests only. The gateway run_detail_value allowlist stays as committed.

The worker policy is rewritten. A paused fold never holds a run on its own (its approval does, through has_pending_approval). Only parks inside the TTL and live claims are spared. Crash-park is restricted to active round-kind folds with clean ledger and approval facts (P6). All worker fold logic sits behind SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED AND SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED. The claim_due_recovery candidate query gets only the S8-0 expiry clause; the original fold_holds and fold_expired predicates are dropped.
S8-0 (P8) is its own first commit, in both approval predicates, with a live-delivery-lease exception, gated under SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED.
Two closed tokens are new: park_not_restorable and park_route_unavailable (gateway frames 22 to 24, executor tokens 17 to 19, SPA parity). No new HTTP code: a non-parked run is 409 not_resumable.
The S8-2 fan-out names all 22 RunAgentResponse literals in 5 files that have no ..Default and break with tag 11.
The SPA and BFF part is split: S8-7a (the contract, before the gateway accepts the shape) and S8-7b (BFF forwarding, ag_ui CUSTOM, display-only handling). continueParkedRun exists with no caller.

P9: the cancel path is verified. cancel_run purges the fold in its transaction; the obligation is superseded by the worker's next supersede_terminalized_obligations pass, not in the cancel transaction. A DB test pins both.
failure_matrix: Park save commits, executor crashes before responding. The user sees agent_run_state_unknown (the stream's existing lost-response handling); the run stays non-terminal and parked. Safe: the worker spares it until the TTL (or terminalizes it at its deadline if park recovery is off), and a park continue resumes it.

Park save is ambiguous (timeout), the executor falls back and finalizes. The user sees the committed typed failure. Safe: transition_managed_run_terminal purges any committed park in the same transaction.
Park save refused (stale, closed, store off, recovery off, cap, TTL, ZDR, content, key). The user sees the committed failure, byte-identical. Safe: no park row is written.

Executor crashes between the worker's crash-park and the user's click. The user sees nothing live (P5); RunDetail.resumable is true for a service reader; a park continue resumes from seq N+1 with the fence at N+2.

Zombie writer after a crash-park. Its next round or pre_effect save gets loop_checkpoint_stale: the writer fails and effects are held. If it finalizes, the run ends and the park is purged; a later continue gets not_resumable. Its in-flight read can finish; no effect starts.

Two park continues with distinct tokens. Exactly one claim wins. The other gets not_claimable (not_resumable), or, if it re-claims a lapsed lease, loses at the fence (Stale, resume_checkpoint_unavailable). Nothing is dispatched twice.
Same token retried within the lease: continue_in_progress. After the lease lapses: a re-claim, and the first attempt (if alive) loses at the fence.

Claim committed, executor dies before the fence. The row stays resuming (kind park, claim live) and is spared by the worker. Once the lease lapses it is re-claimable by an empty ref, still inside the TTL.

Fence saved, executor dies mid-round. The row is active and kind pre_effect or round, depending on progress. At the deadline the worker crash-parks a round-kind fold with clean facts and terminalizes anything else, outcome_unknown.

Resume racing the TTL terminalization. Both lock runs FOR UPDATE: either the worker terminalizes and purges (the claim gets run_ended, not_resumable) or the claim wins (the worker sees a live claim and spares). Never both.

Resume racing a cancel. The claim first: the cancel commits and purges, the fence gets run_ended (Closed), resume_checkpoint_unavailable, nothing dispatched; the finalize of a cancelled run is refused as today. The cancel first: the claim gets run_ended, not_resumable.

Route cannot be rebuilt (kill switch off, connection id missing, provider mismatch). The user sees park_route_unavailable. Safe: no default route, no close; the lease lapses and the park can be resumed later or ends at the TTL.

Structurally unrestorable park (tombstone, open round, pending mismatch, budget spent, digest mismatch). The user sees park_not_restorable. The fold is closed best-effort, so the worker terminalizes it honestly when it is due.
Prompt or tool drift. The user sees park_not_restorable with no close; it is retryable after a fix and ends at the TTL otherwise.
Recovery switch turned off with parks live. At each run's deadline the committed worker terminalizes it as outcome_unknown and purges it. Nothing is stranded.
Store switch turned off with parks live. The same as the row above. Claims are refused as loop_checkpoint_disabled (continue_disabled).
Gateway older than the executor. Status parked reaches the Unknown arm (RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED): the user sees an unknown state while the run is parked. Avoided by the deploy order.
A pending cold delivery whose approval expired mid-delivery (S8-0). The live delivery lease keeps sparing the run; once the lease lapses, the run is recovered as outcome_unknown.

findings.issue: The park branch launches with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent and no pre-consume. In agentic_run_stream the dispatch-error arms that exempt a continuation from terminalization all key on spend.is_spent(), so a refused or unreachable park continue terminalizes the parked run and purges its fold. The design never mentions this arm order. Two cases: (1) The executor answers a park request with InvalidArgument (resume_incomplete, when executor parking is off) or PermissionDenied (Refusal::Forbidden, resume_forbidden). Both are 'confirmed rejections'. The gateway calls terminalize_agent_dispatch_rejection_authenticated, which records a Failed terminal receipt, and the fold goes with it. (2) The executor is unreachable (ECONNREFUSED). The dispatch_never_reached_execution_core arm terminalizes the run as agent_dispatch_unreachable. That is the normal moment to click Continue on a crash-parked run: the executor has just crashed and is restarting. This also breaks the documented flip order (gateway on, executor off) and any executor rollback while parks exist.
findings.evidence: agentic_run_stream arms in order: (a) `Ok(Ok(Err(status))) if spend.is_spent()` never terminalizes; (b) `if is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection(&status)` (InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied) terminalizes with AgentDispatchFailure::Rejected; (c) the `continuing && !spend.is_spent()` arm handles only FailedPrecondition, Aborted, NotFound and the ZDR trailer, because classify_continue_dispatch_failure runs after (b); (d) `dispatch_never_reached_execution_core` terminalizes with AgentDispatchFailure::Unreachable. The comment above (c) says InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied 'took the confirmed-rejection arm above'. grpc.rs enforce_resume returns Status::invalid_argument("resume_incomplete"). resume.rs Refusal::Forbidden.status() is permission_denied. The design's gateway section says only 'launch with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the park continue its own regime in agentic_run_stream: no arm may terminalize a run whose resume.mode is 'park'. A refusal becomes a typed frame via classify_continue_dispatch_failure, and an unreachable executor becomes continue_unreachable with the run left parked. This needs an ApprovalSpend-style discriminator, or a guard on arms (b), (d) and the 'request construction rejected' arm. Add handler-level tests per gRPC code (InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated, ECONNREFUSED) that assert no terminal receipt and a fold that survives. Reorder the flip so the gateway never accepts the park shape before the executor does.

findings.issue: A park resume silently shrinks the run's round budget to the gateway's default-route budget, so a parked pinned run (the only kind that parks, per P5) can exhaust or be closed at once. The gateway's continue launch uses AgentRoute::default(), so run_budget_from_env(false) sends AGENTIC_MAX_ROUNDS, not the AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_ROUNDS the pinned run started with. effective_authority takes min(fold budget, request budget), and apply_authority writes it to req.max_rounds, which the loop reads. The design never says where the budget comes from (INV-05: 'values come from the fold, never from request or replica state').
findings.evidence: effective_authority: `effective.max_rounds = effective.max_rounds.min(resolved_max_rounds(req.max_rounds))`. run_budget.rs: subscription budget 'wins over' the general one on a pinned route and is meant to differ; the gateway test a_subscription_turn_gets_the_subscription_budget uses 10 vs 6. spawn_run_dispatch: `run_budget_from_env(route.is_pinned())`, and continue_run passes AgentRoute::default(). Result: a run pinned with a budget of 10 that parked at round 7 resumes with a budget of 6. `while rounds_executed + delegated_rounds < max_rounds` never runs, the loop returns Exhausted, and finalize records a failed run after the user's click. If check (d) 'rounds_executed + delegated < resolved max_rounds' uses the narrowed value, it instead fails structurally, close_rpc closes the fold, and the run is terminalized later. The design leaves it open whether (d) compares to the fold's or the narrowed budget.
findings.suggested_fix: On the park path, take max_rounds from fold.authority exactly (do not min with the request placeholder). Evaluate (d) against that value. Add a test: fold budget 10, request budget 6, parked at round 7, which resumes and runs rounds 8..10.

findings.issue: CrashPark can duplicate the final assistant message. finalize appends the assistant message (AppendMessage) and only then records the terminal receipt. These are two separate RPCs, not one transaction. If the executor dies between them, or record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome fails and finalize returns Err (token unavailable, session-core down), the thread already holds the answer and the run is non-terminal. The committed worker ends it as outcome_unknown. The new worker sees an active round fold (the answering round saves nothing, so the fold is from the previous tool round), with no pending approval, no ledger row at or after fold.updated_at and no open reservation, so every crash fact is clean and it CrashParks. A resume re-infers the final round and finalize appends a second assistant message. The ledger and approval facts cannot see this effect.
findings.evidence: agent.rs finalize: step 3 `session.append_message(...)` (for !req.zdr && refusal.is_none()), step 4 `record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome(...).await?`. run_rounds: `if response.tool_calls.is_empty() { answer = Some(..); break; }` saves nothing, and save_round runs only at the end of a tool round. The CrashFacts in the design are {pending_approval_any_expiry, ledger_after_fold, ledger_open} plus fold content; none looks at the thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a crash fact: no assistant message on the run's thread created at or after fold.updated_at (session-core owns messages), and Terminalize otherwise. Alternatively make finalize idempotent per run (a deterministic message key). Add a DB test that seeds an assistant message after the fold and expects Terminalize.

findings.issue: A park resume re-derives the offered tools from a request that carries no client tools, but the original run's tool set includes the client-declared tools. Any run launched with client tools can never be resumed. Every attempt ends in park_not_restorable (design step f, deliberately without close), while RunDetail.resumable is true until the TTL. Even without client tools, merged_tool_defs includes best-effort MCP listing and policy-resolved tools, so a transient listing difference also makes the run unrestorable. The fold stores only names (authority.tool_names) and the prompt digest, not the definitions. The approval flow avoids this by retaining full definitions in the approval snapshot.
findings.evidence: run_agent: `merged_tool_defs(&req.run_id, ..., &req.tools, capability_policy, ...)` folds in client tools via append_untrusted_tool_defs. The gateway sends them (build_run_agent_request: `tools: tools.to_vec()`; the SPA sends createSelectedAgentToolSpecs). continue_run launches with `Vec::new()` tools. The design check (f) demands equality with fold.authority.tool_names and prompt_digest_of. The offered set is also re-resolved from live MCP and capability-policy state: `client.list_tools(...)` and `resolve_server_tool_definitions(...)`, both best-effort.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (1) store the offered tool definitions in the park fold (the approval snapshot already caps them at 64 KiB) and resume from them, or (2) make parkable() require req.tools.is_empty() and a tool set derivable on resume, and say so. Add a test with a run that has client tools: either it parks and resumes, or it does not park.

findings.issue: P6 is not met: crash-parking is dormant only on the two session-core switches, and the worker cannot tell whether anything can resume the park. One switch, SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED, gates the S8-0 expiry fix, executor park saves and crash-parking. An operator who turns it on for the expiry fix, or for executor parks, also crash-parks every clean active round fold of every run while the gateway or executor parking may still be off. Those runs hang up to 24 h, invisible and unresumable, where the committed worker ends them in about 15 minutes. The documented flip order puts SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED first, so crash-parks exist before the gateway or executor can resume them. Crash-park applies to unpinned folds without any marker that an executor with parking on wrote them, since route ids are required only when pinned.
findings.evidence: Design recover_claimed_terminalization: `if loop_checkpoint::enabled() && park_recovery_enabled()` is the only condition. decide_hold: the CrashPark condition 'authority.provider_hint empty, or the route_connection_id extension present' needs no executor marker for unpinned runs. DEPLOY ORDER: 'FLIP ORDER: SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED, then EXECUTION_LOOP_PARKING_ENABLED on the gateway, then on the executor'. Risk 1 in the design admits crash parks are invisible to the UI.
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Crash-park only a fold carrying an executor marker that is written only when parking_active() (for example always write route_model, or a dedicated extension, for every fold under parking, pinned or not). (2) Give S8-0 its own switch or ship it ungated, and give crash-park its own sub-switch. (3) Flip order: gateway, then executor, then SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED last.

findings.issue: park_until is never enforced, so a normal early click spends one of the five parks. The empty-ref claim ignores park_until, as the checklist notes ('claim() does not check park_until today'). An early Continue for a provider that is still exhausted resumes, fences, infers, fails and parks again at parks+1 with a fresh park_until. Five early clicks make the run fail for good (park_limit_reached falls back to the committed failure). The gateway cannot gate it, because run_detail_value hides park fields.
findings.evidence: Design CLAIM_PARK_SQL: `WHERE run_id=$1 AND kind='park' AND (state='parked' OR (state='resuming' AND claim_expires_at < now()))`. No park_until predicate. MAX_PARKS_PER_RUN = 5. Checklist crash_windows[17].
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse the claim before park_until with a closed token (not_claimable, or a new park_not_due in the vocabulary). Or make an unchanged-reason re-park not count against the cap. Add a DB test.

findings.issue: The 'upgrade of a failure' claim is false where it matters. A parked run gets no persisted explanation, the run read hides the park, and TTL expiry ends the run as outcome_unknown, where the committed outcome for the same stop is a typed, worded failure with a persisted explanation. The gateway appends an assistant explanation for a typed subscription failure; the park arm sends only a frame. After a reload the thread shows nothing and RunDetail through the gateway shows a running run. A never-resumed park ends 24 h later as outcome_unknown / reconciliation_required although nothing is unknown.
findings.evidence: agentic_run_stream Failed arm: `append_assistant_message_authenticated(.. &message ..)` for a typed subscription failure; the design's Parked arm only 'publishes the RUN_PARKED envelope and sends Event run_parked'. The design keeps http_routes run_detail_value without resumable or park_reason. The TTL path uses apply_managed_terminal_outcome(Failed("outcome_unknown")). Checklist crash_windows[16]: 'a typed failure is shown on reconnect'.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a worded park explanation at park time (as the typed failure does), and at TTL expiry record a failure code derived from park_reason (provider_unavailable or similar) instead of outcome_unknown for executor parks. Alternatively state that S8 must not be flipped before a UI path exists, and gate executor parking separately from crash-park.

findings.issue: The park resume fence is a pre_effect fold with no open round, and decide_hold terminalizes every pre_effect and fence fold. A crash anywhere between the fence and the first end-of-round save (the whole first inference and every read tool of the resumed run) ends the run as outcome_unknown, although no effect can have run. The user's click is spent and the recovery path (crash-park) is closed to exactly the window just after a resume.
findings.evidence: fold.rs fence_with hard-codes SaveKind::PreEffect. Design S8-5: `folds.save_fence(build_fold(snapshot, None, None))`. Design decide_hold: 'every other active fold, including pre_effect folds, every fence fold and every open round: Terminalize'.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark a park fence (extension, or a round-kind fence save with round None, pending None). Let decide_hold CrashPark it under the same clean ledger and approval facts. Add a test: crash after the fence, then CrashPark, then resume.

findings.issue: The design adds a second launch and a second read of the resume switch inside continue_run. Existing source-scan tests pin the structure of that function, so S8-6 will not pass alone unless those tests are deliberately rewritten, and the lead's binding says one /continue route and one AgentResume literal.
findings.evidence: continue_run_consumes_through_the_spawned_helper_after_the_preflight asserts `body.matches("agentic_run_stream(").count() == 1` ('one launch, one stream call') and `body.matches("loop_resume_enabled(").count() == 1` ('the switch is read once'). The design's park branch needs its own launch and its own `loop_resume_enabled(), else continue_disabled` check.
findings.suggested_fix: Restructure so the park branch builds `resume` and `spend` and reuses the single `launch` closure and the single switch read. Update the pinned tests explicitly in S8-6 and say so.

findings.issue: Gaps in the crash-park facts. decide_hold and park_crashed never check rounds_executed + delegated_rounds against authority.max_rounds. A fold written at the last round is crash-parked, then fails the executor's check (d), is closed and is terminalized, after a 24 h invisible hang. An unpinned fold without route_model resumes with an empty requested model (route_request takes the extension, which is absent), so model selection can drift from the original run.
findings.evidence: Design CrashFacts lists approvals, ledger and fold-content checks, not the budget. route_request: 'req.model = the route_model extension'; the extension is required only for pinned folds.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the budget check to park_crashed (terminalize at once when no round is left). Require route_model for every crash-parked fold (see the marker finding).

findings.issue: Small mismatches with the lead decisions and the source, to record. (1) P1 says the empty-ref claim matches state parked ONLY; the design also claims a lapsed 'resuming' park. This is justified and safe (the fence CAS decides), but it is a deviation the owner should confirm. (2) P8 asks for the expiry fix as a plain separate commit; the design gates it, so the stranding persists at default (listed as an open question). (3) The design states 22 RunAgentResponse literals with no ..Default; I count 17 same-line construction sites in 5 files, and 23 matches of the type name (6 are signatures, impls and mentions). The build will find every site, but the stated number is wrong. (4) The park write at the credential-margin loop top can spend up to GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT (10 s) of the 60 s CREDENTIAL_MARGIN before the committed fallback finalize runs. (5) The RUN_PARKED envelope plus the executor's RunParked orchestration event plus the step-update arm may show a client the same park twice.
findings.evidence: claim SQL in design vs P1; run_budget CREDENTIAL_MARGIN 60 s vs fold.rs GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT 10 s; grep of RunAgentResponse literal sites; agentic_run_stream follow_agentic_run step updates.
findings.suggested_fix: Record (1) and (2) in the ledger as owner-confirmed. Correct the literal count to what the build reports. Use ROUND_SAVE_TIMEOUT (2 s) for a park attempted under the credential cause. De-duplicate the RunParked projection (frame or event, not both) for the same client.

checked: Verified against committed source: run_rounds loop-top order (is_stopped, refusal.latched, deadline.expired, heartbeat) and the inference Err arm. findings.issue: P6 is violated. Lead decision P6 says crash-parking must not delay terminalization of runs that nothing can resume. In this design the worker crash-parks whenever SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED are on. Those are session-core switches only; nothing checks that the gateway or executor parking/resume switches are on, and no UI path exists (P10). The design's own flip order turns SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED on FIRST, before EXECUTION_LOOP_PARKING_ENABLED on the gateway and executor. During that window every crashed run whose last fold is a clean round fold is crash-parked and kept up to the TTL (24 h). The committed worker ends such a run about 15 minutes after its last heartbeat. Risk 1 admits this and does not fix it.

(2) The budget is resolve_run_budget(route.is_pinned() = false), which uses AGENTIC_MAX_ROUNDS and not AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_ROUNDS. effective_authority then narrows max_rounds to min(fold, request). blocking.issue: The park branch launches with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent and no pre-consume. In agentic_run_stream the dispatch-error arms that exempt a continuation from terminalization all key on spend.is_spent(), so a refused or unreachable park continue terminalizes the parked run and purges its fold. The design never mentions this arm order. Two cases: (1) The executor answers a park request with InvalidArgument (resume_incomplete, when executor parking is off) or PermissionDenied (Refusal::Forbidden, resume_forbidden). Both are 'confirmed rejections'. The gateway calls terminalize_agent_dispatch_rejection_authenticated, which records a Failed terminal receipt, and the fold goes with it. (2) The executor is unreachable (ECONNREFUSED). The dispatch_never_reached_execution_core arm terminalizes the run as agent_dispatch_unreachable. That is the normal moment to click Continue on a crash-parked run: the executor has just crashed and is restarting. This also breaks the documented flip order (gateway on, executor off) and any executor rollback while parks exist.
blocking.evidence: agentic_run_stream arms in order: (a) `Ok(Ok(Err(status))) if spend.is_spent()` never terminalizes; (b) `if is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection(&status)` (InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied) terminalizes with AgentDispatchFailure::Rejected; (c) the `continuing && !spend.is_spent()` arm handles only FailedPrecondition, Aborted, NotFound and the ZDR trailer, because classify_continue_dispatch_failure runs after (b); (d) `dispatch_never_reached_execution_core` terminalizes with AgentDispatchFailure::Unreachable. The comment above (c) says InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied 'took the confirmed-rejection arm above'. grpc.rs enforce_resume returns Status::invalid_argument("resume_incomplete"). resume.rs Refusal::Forbidden.status() is permission_denied. The design's gateway section says only 'launch with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent'.
blocking.suggested_fix: Give the park continue its own regime in agentic_run_stream: no arm may terminalize a run whose resume.mode is 'park'. A refusal becomes a typed frame via classify_continue_dispatch_failure, and an unreachable executor becomes continue_unreachable with the run left parked. This needs an ApprovalSpend-style discriminator, or a guard on arms (b), (d) and the 'request construction rejected' arm. Add handler-level tests per gRPC code (InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated, ECONNREFUSED) that assert no terminal receipt and a fold that survives. Reorder the flip so the gateway never accepts the park shape before the executor does.

blocking.issue: A park resume silently shrinks the run's round budget to the gateway's default-route budget, so a parked pinned run (the only kind that parks, per P5) can exhaust or be closed at once. The gateway's continue launch uses AgentRoute::default(), so run_budget_from_env(false) sends AGENTIC_MAX_ROUNDS, not the AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_ROUNDS the pinned run started with. effective_authority takes min(fold budget, request budget), and apply_authority writes it to req.max_rounds, which the loop reads. The design never says where the budget comes from (INV-05: 'values come from the fold, never from request or replica state').
blocking.evidence: effective_authority: `effective.max_rounds = effective.max_rounds.min(resolved_max_rounds(req.max_rounds))`. run_budget.rs: subscription budget 'wins over' the general one on a pinned route and is meant to differ; the gateway test a_subscription_turn_gets_the_subscription_budget uses 10 vs 6. spawn_run_dispatch: `run_budget_from_env(route.is_pinned())`, and continue_run passes AgentRoute::default(). Result: a run pinned with a budget of 10 that parked at round 7 resumes with a budget of 6. `while rounds_executed + delegated_rounds < max_rounds` never runs, the loop returns Exhausted, and finalize records a failed run after the user's click. If check (d) 'rounds_executed + delegated < resolved max_rounds' uses the narrowed value, it instead fails structurally, close_rpc closes the fold, and the run is terminalized later. The design leaves it open whether (d) compares to the fold's or the narrowed budget.
blocking.suggested_fix: On the park path, take max_rounds from fold.authority exactly (do not min with the request placeholder). Evaluate (d) against that value. Add a test: fold budget 10, request budget 6, parked at round 7, which resumes and runs rounds 8..10.

blocking.issue: CrashPark can duplicate the final assistant message. finalize appends the assistant message (AppendMessage) and only then records the terminal receipt. These are two separate RPCs, not one transaction. If the executor dies between them, or record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome fails and finalize returns Err (token unavailable, session-core down), the thread already holds the answer and the run is non-terminal. The committed worker ends it as outcome_unknown. The new worker sees an active round fold (the answering round saves nothing, so the fold is from the previous tool round), with no pending approval, no ledger row at or after fold.updated_at and no open reservation, so every crash fact is clean and it CrashParks. A resume re-infers the final round and finalize appends a second assistant message. The ledger and approval facts cannot see this effect.
blocking.evidence: agent.rs finalize: step 3 `session.append_message(...)` (for !req.zdr && refusal.is_none()), step 4 `record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome(...).await?`. run_rounds: `if response.tool_calls.is_empty() { answer = Some(..); break; }` saves nothing, and save_round runs only at the end of a tool round. The CrashFacts in the design are {pending_approval_any_expiry, ledger_after_fold, ledger_open} plus fold content; none looks at the thread.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a crash fact: no assistant message on the run's thread created at or after fold.updated_at (session-core owns messages), and Terminalize otherwise. Alternatively make finalize idempotent per run (a deterministic message key). Add a DB test that seeds an assistant message after the fold and expects Terminalize.

blocking.issue: A park resume re-derives the offered tools from a request that carries no client tools, but the original run's tool set includes the client-declared tools. Any run launched with client tools can never be resumed. Every attempt ends in park_not_restorable (design step f, deliberately without close), while RunDetail.resumable is true until the TTL. Even without client tools, merged_tool_defs includes best-effort MCP listing and policy-resolved tools, so a transient listing difference also makes the run unrestorable. The fold stores only names (authority.tool_names) and the prompt digest, not the definitions. The approval flow avoids this by retaining full definitions in the approval snapshot.
blocking.evidence: run_agent: `merged_tool_defs(&req.run_id, ..., &req.tools, capability_policy, ...)` folds in client tools via append_untrusted_tool_defs. The gateway sends them (build_run_agent_request: `tools: tools.to_vec()`; the SPA sends createSelectedAgentToolSpecs). continue_run launches with `Vec::new()` tools. The design check (f) demands equality with fold.authority.tool_names and prompt_digest_of. The offered set is also re-resolved from live MCP and capability-policy state: `client.list_tools(...)` and `resolve_server_tool_definitions(...)`, both best-effort.
blocking.suggested_fix: Either (1) store the offered tool definitions in the park fold (the approval snapshot already caps them at 64 KiB) and resume from them, or (2) make parkable() require req.tools.is_empty() and a tool set derivable on resume, and say so. Add a test with a run that has client tools: either it parks and resumes, or it does not park.

blocking.issue: P6 is not met: crash-parking is dormant only on the two session-core switches, and the worker cannot tell whether anything can resume the park. One switch, SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED, gates the S8-0 expiry fix, executor park saves and crash-parking. An operator who turns it on for the expiry fix, or for executor parks, also crash-parks every clean active round fold of every run while the gateway or executor parking may still be off. Those runs hang up to 24 h, invisible and unresumable, where the committed worker ends them in about 15 minutes. The documented flip order puts SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED first, so crash-parks exist before the gateway or executor can resume them. Crash-park applies to unpinned folds without any marker that an executor with parking on wrote them, since route ids are required only when pinned.
blocking.evidence: Design recover_claimed_terminalization: `if loop_checkpoint::enabled() && park_recovery_enabled()` is the only condition. decide_hold: the CrashPark condition 'authority.provider_hint empty, or the route_connection_id extension present' needs no executor marker for unpinned runs. DEPLOY ORDER: 'FLIP ORDER: SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED, then EXECUTION_LOOP_PARKING_ENABLED on the gateway, then on the executor'. Risk 1 in the design admits crash parks are invisible to the UI.
blocking.suggested_fix: (1) Crash-park only a fold carrying an executor marker that is written only when parking_active() (for example always write route_model, or a dedicated extension, for every fold under parking, pinned or not). (2) Give S8-0 its own switch or ship it ungated, and give crash-park its own sub-switch. (3) Flip order: gateway, then executor, then SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED last.

blocking.issue: P6 is violated. Lead decision P6 says crash-parking must not delay terminalization of runs that nothing can resume. revised.summary:
S8 turns a small set of typed, content-free, recoverable stops of a root Do loop into a durable park. A park is an encrypted fold of kind "park", written at a round boundary; RunAgentResponse.status is "parked" with park_reason. A parked run is resumed through the existing POST /continue route by a body with a claim_token and an EXACTLY empty approval_id.

Parking upgrades a failure; it is never a new way to fail. If the park cannot be written, the run gets exactly the committed outcome. A park continue never terminalizes a run: whatever the executor answers, and also when the executor cannot be reached, the run stays parked and the client gets a typed frame with nothing spent.

What parks (pinned runs only in the first merge, P5):
- credential_window: a DeadlineCause::Credential at the loop top.
- provider_exhausted: subscription_usage_limit, or rate_limited WITH retry_after_ms.
- upstream_unavailable: subscription_upstream_unavailable.
- reauth_required: subscription_reauth_required.

What stays a failure: everything else (WallClock, rate_limited without timing, bad_request, prompt_too_long, route_unavailable, Exhausted, unpinned untyped failures, a latched refusal after the loop). A run whose offered tools cannot be re-derived on resume (client tools, or MCP-listed tools) never parks.

Changes from v3:
1. A park continue has its own non-terminalizing regime in agentic_run_stream. It is placed right after the spent arm and is detected from the gateway's own resume mode. A confirmed rejection, an unreachable executor or a construction failure therefore leaves the run parked.
2. A park resume takes max_rounds from the fold's authority exactly; it is not narrowed by the gateway's unpinned placeholder. The gateway words a pinned failure_code and follows a park continue with the pinned deadline.
3. Crash-park needs a new crash fact: no message on the run's thread at or after the fold's updated_at. This stops a crash between finalize's AppendMessage and its terminal receipt from being re-inferred into a second answer.
4. The tool set is re-derived on resume from built-ins plus server-resolved tools only, and runs that had client or MCP tools are not parkable.
5. The switches are separate:
   - S8-0 has its own SESSION_CORE_RECOVERY_APPROVAL_EXPIRY_ENABLED.
   - SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED accepts and spares executor parks.
   - A new SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED, flipped LAST, crash-parks only folds that carry the executor's parking marker (the route_model extension, written under parking for every fold, pinned or not).
6. The flip order is: session-core park recovery, then the gateway, then the executor, then crash-park.
7. The RunResumed key is resumed_segment, so sse.rs still names segment_no once. The segment is computed in park.rs, so agent.rs never contains ".segment_no".
8. Every committed guard and test that S8 breaks is listed against the step that breaks it, including seed_fold for kind park.

run_agent_with_tools park path (resume.mode == "park"), in order, before any route use:
- a. Widening checks: the request names no route (provider_hint and subscription_connection_id empty, else authority_route_mismatch), no Space (else authority_space_mismatch), and no ZDR waiver (else durable_mutation_forbidden).
- b. Switch checks: parking_active() && checkpoint_enabled() && ledger_enabled(), else continue_disabled. in_place_writer_off(..) must be None, else not_resumable.
- c. park::claim_parked: ClaimLoopCheckpoint{pause_ref: "", claim_token}. classify_park_claim maps the outcome:
  - claim_held -> continue_in_progress;
  - run_ended or not_claimable -> not_resumable;
  - PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated -> resume_forbidden;
  - the ZDR trailer -> durable_mutation_forbidden;
  - disabled -> continue_disabled;
  - unreadable or InvalidArgument -> park_not_restorable;
  - anything else -> resume_checkpoint_unavailable.
- d. park::check_park_fold(claimed, run_id) checks: kind park, the run, claimed segment == fold.segment_no, is_resumable, effect_ledger, system first, the authority digest, pending Park, round_in_flight None, rounds_executed + delegated < fold.authority.max_rounds (the FOLD's own budget, which is immutable, so a failure is genuinely structural), and no Space. A structural failure gives a best-effort close_rpc(seq, "park_not_restorable") and then the refusal.
- e. park::route_request(req, fold):
  - req.model = EXT_ROUTE_MODEL;
  - for a pinned authority: provider_hint = PROVIDER_ID and connection = EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION (missing gives park_route_unavailable);
  - plan_mode from the fold;
  - then ModelRoute::resolve(..). Err, a provider mismatch or a waived route gives park_route_unavailable, with NO close and never a default route (P2).
- f. Tools: park::derivable_tool_defs(..). Names must equal fold.authority.tool_names and prompt_digest_of(compose_system_prompt(names), tools) == fold.prompt_digest. A mismatch (a transient server-resolved outage or deploy skew) gives park_not_restorable WITHOUT close.
- g. Authority: effective = effective_authority(&fold.authority, &route_req)?, then effective.max_rounds = fold.authority.max_rounds. This is the one documented exception to the min: the request's max_rounds on a park continue is the gateway's unpinned default placeholder, not a user narrowing. Then apply_authority; mode = resolve_mode(fold.authority.mode).
- h. deadline = RunDeadline::for_run(now, .., route.is_pinned(), the NEW request's bearers), so a credential_window park resumes under fresh credentials.
- i. run_agent_with_route(.., Some(ParkClaim)). The new trailing parameter is None at every committed call site.

risks: The UI cannot see parks: run_detail_value excludes resumable and park_reason, crash parks emit no live event (P5), and there is no button (P10). Mitigation: SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED is a separate switch, flipped last and only with the owner's go-ahead, so with it off no crash-crashed run is held past the committed ~15 minutes. Executor parks are only held where the gateway and executor can resume them by API.

The park path is the one place max_rounds is not min'd with the request. This is justified because the continue request carries the gateway's unpinned default placeholder (AgentRoute::default, run_budget_from_env(false)), not a user narrowing, and the fold's budget was itself bounded at run start. A future gateway that sends a real narrowing on a park continue must revisit park_authority.

Deriving the park regime from the resume mode in agentic_run_stream relies on the resume being built only by the gateway's own continue_resume (the one literal guard). A second construction site would need the same discriminator.
The thread-message crash fact is conservative: a user posting a new message on the thread after the fold also blocks a crash-park, and that run is terminalized as committed. This is accepted.

A live but silent loop (more than 15 minutes) can be crash-parked under itself. The seq+1 re-seal fences its next save, so its effects are held; it can still finalize, which purges the park. A resume is fenced against it.
The ledger has no per-attempt owner, so P6's release-owner check is conservative: no ledger row at or after the fold's updated_at, no open reservation, and never a pre_effect or fence fold.

Runs offered client or MCP tools never park (tools_derivable). That is most SPA Do turns that send createSelectedAgentToolSpecs, so in practice S8 first helps API and built-in-only runs. Storing the definitions in the fold is a later option, open for the owner.
Server-resolved tool skew (a transient policy outage) at resume gives park_not_restorable without a close; it is retryable and ends at the TTL otherwise.
An ambiguous park save can commit while the executor falls back and finalizes; the terminal transition purges it, and a CHECKPOINT_SAVED park event remains in the audit trail.
Lock order: the park claim takes runs, then outbox, then fold, which is the worker's order; save and cancel take runs then fold. This is verified by reading, not by a stress test.
Weekly usage limits that reset beyond the TTL are refused at save and fail as today.
The BFF has no switch: an absent approval_id key now forwards and ends as the gateway's 400 continue_incomplete with gateway parking off. Accepted, since no UI calls it.
Gateway/executor skew is handled by the deploy order and by the park regime: an executor that does not know park answers resume_incomplete, which is a typed frame, never a terminalization.
Sandbox leases are not released on a park; WorkspaceStateLost is handled by the S7 closers.
invariants: A park is an upgrade of a failure: if the park fold is not durably written, the outcome is byte-identical to the committed one.
A park continue never terminalizes a run. Every executor refusal, an unreachable executor and a request-construction failure leave the run parked, with a typed frame and nothing spent.
Only typed, content-free evidence parks. rate_limited parks only with retry_after_ms; WallClock never parks.
Zero-retention, waived, Space, delegated and stage-1-segment runs never park, keep a fold, or get claimed or resumed.
A park sits at a round boundary and returns before finalize: no receipt, no append, no ledger finalization, no lease release.
An empty pause_ref claims only a kind='park' row, never a pause fold; there is one parked fold per run.
A park resume saves its fence at the claimed seq before the first inference and before any dispatch.
A park resume runs on the route rebuilt from the fold's identifiers or not at all, under the fold's own round budget and authority; it never runs on a default route.
A park resume offers exactly the tools derivable without MCP or client input, equal to the fold's tool names and prompt digest.

A widened /continue is refused, not narrowed. There is one AgentResume literal, one launch and one resume-switch read in continue_run. segment_no 0 is sent and ignored; sse.rs names segment_no once; agent.rs and grpc.rs never contain `.segment_no`.

Crash-park covers only an active round-kind fold that carries the executor parking marker (route_model), with no open round, no pending approval of any expiry, no unaccounted ledger row and no thread message at or after the fold. It runs only with SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED. A fold whose approval is consumed is never crash-parked or restored.
Receipts are immutable: TTL expiry and every non-spared case go through the unmodified apply_managed_terminal_outcome.
With every S8 switch off, behaviour is committed: no park RPC, no fold extension, the committed claim SQL, no worker fold query, no new frame. The one recorded exception is the BFF's absent-key form.
Park, event, frame and log fields are ids, counts, closed tokens and timestamps only; folds stay ciphertext under AAD (run, org, user, seq); route identifiers are not credentials.
The Model proposes and Quarry executes: parking never touches browser_agent or Quarry state.

failure_matrix: Park save commits, then the executor crashes before responding. The user sees agent_run_state_unknown; the run is parked. Safe: it is spared until the TTL, and a park continue resumes it.
Park save is ambiguous and the executor falls back and finalizes. The user sees the committed typed failure. Safe: the terminal transition purges any park.
Park save is refused (any reason). The user sees the committed failure, byte-identical. Safe: no row is written.
Park continue while the executor is down (ECONNREFUSED). The user sees continue_unreachable, nothing spent. Safe: no terminalization and the fold survives; retry later.
Park continue refused by an executor with parking off (resume_incomplete) or by a permission check (resume_forbidden). The user sees the typed frame. Safe: the run stays parked.
Park continue whose request cannot be built locally. The user sees continue_refused. Safe: nothing is sent or terminalized.

Executor crashes between finalize's AppendMessage and the terminal receipt. The user sees the answer in the thread; the run stays non-terminal until the deadline. Safe: the thread-message fact gives Terminalize outcome_unknown, never a crash-park and never a second answer.
Executor crashes mid-run, with crash-park on, the fold clean and the marker present. The user sees nothing live; a park continue resumes from seq N+1 with the fence at N+2.
Executor crashes mid-run, with crash-park off. Committed: outcome_unknown about 15 minutes after the last heartbeat.
Zombie writer after a crash-park. Its next save is loop_checkpoint_stale and its effects are held; if it finalizes, the park is purged and a later continue gets not_resumable.
Two park continues with distinct tokens. One claim wins; the other gets not_resumable, or loses at the fence (resume_checkpoint_unavailable). Nothing is dispatched twice.
Same token retried within the lease: continue_in_progress. After the lease lapses: a re-claim, and the old attempt loses at the fence.
Claim committed, executor dies before the fence. The row is resuming and spared; once the lease lapses it can be re-claimed inside the TTL.
Fence saved, executor dies mid-round. At the deadline: a round-kind fold with clean facts is crash-parked (if on); anything else is terminalized outcome_unknown.
Resume racing the TTL terminalization. Both take runs FOR UPDATE: either terminalized (the claim gets not_resumable) or claimed (spared). Never both.

Resume racing a cancel. Claim first: the fence gets run_ended, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, nothing dispatched. Cancel first: the claim gets not_resumable. The obligation ends at the next supersede pass.
Route cannot be rebuilt. The user sees park_route_unavailable; no default route, no close; retry or TTL.
Tool or prompt drift, or a server-resolved outage at resume. The user sees park_not_restorable without a close; retryable.
Structurally unrestorable park (tombstone, open round, pending mismatch, the fold's budget spent, digest mismatch). The user sees park_not_restorable; the fold is closed and terminalized when due.
Park recovery or the store switch turned off with parks live. Committed worker: outcome_unknown at the deadline, purged; claims get continue_disabled.
Crash-park switch turned off. No new crash-parks; existing parks are spared until the TTL, then terminalized.
Gateway parking on, executor off (flip step 2). A park continue is a typed resume_incomplete frame; no executor parks exist yet.
A cold delivery whose approval expired mid-delivery (S8-0). The live delivery lease keeps the run spared; after it lapses, outcome_unknown.
